---
title: "Training and monitoring a surrogate"
---

Complete the [quickstart](../package/quickstart.qmd) first. Both Python and
Hydra use `Surrogate.fit`, the same model presets and the same artifact formats.

```bash
uv run metis train model=mlp training.steps=1000 plot.enabled=true
uv run metis train model=transformer training.steps=1000
uv run metis train model=flow_matching training.steps=1000 evaluation.n_samples=100
```

The optional figure requires the `[plots]` extra. Add it with `uv add` as shown
in the quickstart. The output directory contains `config.yaml`, `history.json`,
`model.pt` and `metrics.json`, plus `evaluation.png` when requested. These runs
use the bundled example; set `dataset=parquet` and its schema for your own bank.

## What a training step means

A step is one AdamW update using a sampled minibatch. It is not an epoch.
`training.learning_rate`, `training.batch_size` and `training.steps` control the
basic budget. The default is float32 CPU training at a constant learning rate.
Validation chooses the best evaluated weights, and `training.patience` can stop
when validation stops improving. Changing the model changes its objective;
compare [original-unit validation metrics](../package/model-choice.qmd), not
raw losses across families.

## Schedules and numerical execution

```bash
uv run metis train training.schedule=warmup_cosine training.warmup_fraction=0.2 training.min_learning_rate=0.000001
uv run metis train training.device=cuda training.precision=bf16
```

The warm-up/cosine schedule rises to `training.learning_rate`, then decays toward
`training.min_learning_rate` over the declared total step budget. Precision
choices are `fp32`, `tf32` and `bf16`; TF32 needs CUDA. Device and precision
availability depend on hardware. `training.compile_model=true` is optional;
`training.deterministic=true` cannot be combined with compilation.

See [distributed execution](../utils/distributed-training.qmd) for multiple
devices and [checkpoints](saving-and-loading.qmd) for interrupted jobs.
W&B is optional and receives live progress through the same callback used by
Python; see the [tracking guide](../package/hydra.qmd#live-tracking).
